subject: social
title: Goods, Services, Money
about: Goods versus services, buyers and sellers, money, prices, jobs and saving, and simple supply-and-demand stories. NC 1.E.1.4 (trade), 1.E.1.2 and 1.E.1.3 (supply and demand).
tip: Name something you bought today and ask: was that a good or a service, and who was the seller?

cards.q: What do we call things people make or grow that you can touch and buy?
cards.note: Apples, shoes and toys are goods. You can hold them in your hands.

cards.q: What do we call work that people do to help others?
cards.note: A haircut, a bus ride and a checkup are services. You cannot hold a service.

cards.q: Is an apple a good or a service?
cards.note: An apple is a good. A farmer grew it and you can hold it.

cards.q: Is a haircut a good or a service?
cards.note: A haircut is work someone does for you, so it is a service.

cards.q: Are shoes a good or a service?
cards.note: Shoes are goods. People made them and you can touch them.

cards.q: Is a bus ride a good or a service?
cards.note: The driver does the work of taking you somewhere, so a ride is a service.

cards.q: Is a doctor checkup a good or a service?
cards.note: The doctor does work to help you stay well, so a checkup is a service.

cards.q: What do we call giving something to get something else?
cards.note: When you give one thing and get another thing back, that is a trade.

cards.q: Why do countries trade with each other?
cards.a: to get things they do not have
cards.note: One country may grow bananas and another may make cars. They trade so both can have bananas and cars.

cards.q: What do we call someone who buys things?
cards.note: When you pay for a snack at the store, you are the buyer.

cards.q: What do we call someone who sells things?
cards.note: The store worker who takes your money is the seller.

cards.q: What do we use to pay for goods and services?
cards.note: Coins and paper bills are money. These coins are a quarter, a dime, a nickel and a penny.

cards.q: What do we call the amount something costs?
cards.note: The price tag tells how much money you need to buy something.

cards.q: What do we call work you do to earn money?
cards.note: Grown-ups go to a job and get paid money for their work.

cards.q: What do we call keeping some money to use later?
cards.note: Putting coins in a piggy bank for later is saving.

cards.q: What is a safe place that keeps people's money?
cards.note: A bank keeps money safe until people need it.

cards.q: On a hot day, do more or fewer people want ice cream?
cards.note: When more people want something, that is more demand.

cards.q: The store is out of your favorite cereal. What can you do?
wrong: wait in the store all night
cards.note: When a store runs out of something, people pick something else.

cards.q: The farm has too many pumpkins to sell. Does the price go up or down?
cards.note: A big supply makes the price lower, so more people will buy.

cards.q: Everyone wants the same new toy. Is it easy or hard to find in stores?
cards.note: When many people want the same thing, stores can run out fast.
